_comment: The whole voiceover script. Each scene is a list of lines; each line is one caption and one voice clip. `speech` (optional) is what the voice says when it should differ from the caption. `pad` (optional) adds extra seconds after the line so an animation can finish. Scene ids must match SCENE_COMPONENTS in src/CganVideo.tsx.

lines.text: A GAN can invent new faces. But which face? You get whatever comes out.
A conditional GAN, or cGAN, lets you ask for what you want.
lines.speech: A conditional GAN, or C GAN, lets you ask for what you want.

lines.text: It was proposed in 2014 by Mehdi Mirza and Simon Osindero, just months after the original GAN.
A normal generator takes only random noise z.
lines.speech: A normal generator takes only random noise, zee.

lines.text: Say you want a face with glasses. All you can do is draw new noise, again and again, and hope.
The generator has no input for “glasses”. The noise decides everything.
The fix is simple. Give both networks one extra input: the condition, y.
lines.speech: The fix is simple. Give both networks one extra input: the condition, why.

lines.text: y can be a class label, like “glasses”, a digit, or a word. Later we'll see it can even be a whole image.
lines.speech: Why can be a class label, like glasses, a digit, or a word. Later we'll see it can even be a whole image.

lines.text: Back to the forger: now a client orders a specific note, a twenty, and the detective checks whether it really looks like a real twenty.
The generator now takes noise z and the condition y, and makes a sample G(z | y).
lines.speech: The generator now takes noise zee and the condition why, and makes a sample, G of zee given why.

lines.text: The training set provides real pairs: an image together with its correct label.
The discriminator sees an image and a label, and answers: is this a real image of that label?
Everything else is the same GAN game, played separately for every value of y.
lines.speech: Everything else is the same GAN game, played separately for every value of why.

lines.text: How do you feed a label into a network? The simplest way is a one-hot vector: all zeros, with a one for the chosen class.
For the generator, the one-hot vector is joined to the noise vector, end to end.
For an image discriminator, the label can be stretched into extra image channels, one plane per class.
Modern models often use a learned label embedding instead, or the projection discriminator, which compares image features with the label embedding.
The condition gives the discriminator a second job.
It must reject images that look fake…
…and also images that look real but don't match their label.
So the generator can't ignore y. A perfect face without glasses still fails when the label says “glasses”.
lines.speech: So the generator can't ignore why. A perfect face without glasses still fails, when the label says glasses.

lines.text: The cGAN objective is the GAN objective, with every D and G conditioned on y.
lines.speech: The C GAN objective is the GAN objective, with every D and G conditioned on why.

lines.text: D maximizes it: real pairs toward one, generated pairs toward zero.
G minimizes it, for whatever label it is asked to draw.
If training succeeds, G's output for each label matches the real data for that label.
Training alternates, just like a regular GAN.
Train D on real images with their true labels, and on fakes made for randomly chosen labels.
Then train G: pick labels, generate, and push D to say “real” for those same labels.
The label always travels with its image. That's the whole trick.
Here is a real cGAN, trained by the code in this project, on numbers with three classes: A, B and C.
lines.speech: Here is a real C GAN, trained by the code in this project, on numbers with three classes: A, B, and C.

lines.text: Each class is its own bump. At the start, the generator ignores the label: all three outputs sit in the same spot.
As training runs, each label's samples move to their own bump.
The blue curve is D for each label: about one half where that class lives…
…and near zero where other classes live. A perfect class C value labeled A is called fake.
Now we can choose: ask for A, B or C, and the same noise lands in the right place.
With faces, the roles split cleanly.
Keep y fixed and change z: you get different faces of the same kind.
lines.speech: Keep why fixed, and change zee: you get different faces of the same kind.

lines.text: Keep z fixed and change y: the same face, with the attribute you asked for.
lines.speech: Keep zee fixed, and change why: the same face, with the attribute you asked for.

lines.text: The condition controls what you asked for; the noise fills in everything else.
The condition doesn't have to be a single label.
A class: BigGAN generates any of 1,000 ImageNet categories on demand.
lines.speech: A class: Big GAN generates any of a thousand ImageNet categories, on demand.

lines.text: A whole image: Pix2Pix turns sketches into photos, or maps into satellite views.
lines.speech: A whole image: Pix to Pix turns sketches into photos, or maps into satellite views.

lines.text: A low-resolution image: super-resolution GANs fill in the missing detail.
Or a sentence: early text-to-image GANs drew birds and flowers from descriptions.
So: a cGAN is a GAN where both players also see the condition y.
lines.speech: So: a C GAN is a GAN where both players also see the condition, why.

lines.text: The discriminator judges whether the image is real and whether it matches y.
lines.speech: The discriminator judges whether the image is real, and whether it matches why.

lines.text: And the generator learns to make exactly what you ask for.
